title: Building an RNN for Text Classification 🏗️
description: Complete walkthrough: load IMDB reviews, build an LSTM model, train and evaluate.

slides.title: IMDB Sentiment Analysis 🎬
slides.content:
# Binary Classification of Movie Reviews

- 25,000 training reviews, 25,000 testing.
- Each review is a sequence of words (integer‑encoded).
- Goal: predict positive (1) or negative (0) sentiment.

We'll use an **Embedding layer** to convert integer words to dense vectors, then an LSTM to process the sequence.

slides.title: Load and Pad Data
slides.content: The reviews have different lengths → pad/truncate to a fixed length.
slides.codeSnippet:
from tensorflow.keras.datasets import imdb
from tensorflow.keras.preprocessing.sequence import pad_sequences

vocab_size = 10000
maxlen = 200
(x_train, y_train), (x_test, y_test) = imdb.load_data(num_words=vocab_size)

x_train = pad_sequences(x_train, maxlen=maxlen, padding='post', truncating='post')
x_test = pad_sequences(x_test, maxlen=maxlen, padding='post', truncating='post')

quizData.question: Why do we pad sequences to the same length?

options.text: To create batches of tensors with consistent shape

quizData.explanation: Neural networks require inputs of uniform shape; padding/truncating ensures all sequences have the same length.

slides.title: Build the Model
slides.codeSnippet:
from tensorflow.keras.models import Sequential
from tensorflow.keras.layers import Embedding, LSTM, Dense

model = Sequential([
    Embedding(input_dim=vocab_size, output_dim=128, input_length=maxlen),
    LSTM(64, return_sequences=False),
    Dense(1, activation='sigmoid')
])
model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='binary_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])
model.summary()

slides.title: Train and Evaluate 🏋️
slides.content:
# Use Callbacks

Training can overfit quickly. Employ early stopping and validation monitoring.

```python
history = model.fit(x_train, y_train, epochs=10, batch_size=64,
                    validation_split=0.2,
                    callbacks=[tf.keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(patience=2)])
```

After training, `model.evaluate(x_test, y_test)` gives test accuracy.

slides.title: Your Turn 🛠️
slides.content: Replace LSTM with GRU or a Bidirectional LSTM. Does test accuracy improve? Also try adding Dropout (via `Dropout` layer after Embedding or `recurrent_dropout` in LSTM).
